text: Why does America punish Iran, when it makes YOUR gas more expensive?
This is Doug. Doug drives a snowmobile.
Punish how?
Iran sits on oil. Oil is money.
But oil is sold in dollars.
And the dollar belongs to America.
America says: buy Iran oil, lose your dollars.
Banks get scared. Buyers run.
This is called sanctions.
America has done this to Iran since 1979.
So Iran is broke?
Not really. China still buys it. On sale.
About eight dollars off, every barrel.
Doug confused.
Then, war. Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz.
One in five barrels of the world's oil goes through here.
Ships stop. Less oil. Higher price. For everyone.
But America has its own oil!
Yes. America makes the most oil on Earth.
But oil has one world price.
Larry's oil company sells at that price too. Larry happy.
Doug poor.
In real life, gas went from $2.98, to $4.56, in under three months.
Wait. So Doug pays for the punishment?
So why do it? No oil money, no missiles.
Sounds smart, right? But it has two big problems.
Problem one: Iran still sells oil, just cheaper.
Problem two: the bill lands at Doug's pump.
Sanctions are a war, without bullets.
And the real weapon is not a missile. It's the dollar.
Since 1944, the whole world trades in America's dollar.
And this is just the tip of the iceberg.
Would you pay more for gas to punish Iran?
